answer: Each round, every account must finish a sequential, memory-hard proof: a function called jade fills a 2 GB scratchpad, the meadow, then walks it in random order for 10 minutes. Steps cannot run in parallel, so an operator trying to harbor 1,000 fakes needs 2 TB of RAM and 1,000 concurrent cores every round, versus one laptop for an honest agent. Validators spot-check random steps; a wrong or late proof forfeits that account's stake. Colluding attackers cannot split the cost, since each seed binds to one account and one round, so no proof can be shared or reused.
